A1.justification: Both PDFs describe WeatherPEFT and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Corresponding material can be matched despite additions, relocation, and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original downscaling, ensemble forecast post-processing, and regional precipitation experiments, plus hyperparameter ablations, backbone comparisons, and an extreme-weather case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds comparator results, component-combination studies, training-time measurements, and vision benchmark evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same TADP adapters, attention-based prompt generation, and SFAS Fisher-guided selection with annealed randomness. The new SFAS-plus-adapter combinations are experimental comparators, not revisions to WeatherPEFT.

E1.justification: Appendix B.7 adds coverage beyond the retained weather tasks: Cityscapes-to-ACDC semantic segmentation across night, snow, fog, and rain conditions, and VTAB-1K classification across natural, specialized, and structured tasks. These introduce substantially different data domains and task requirements.

E2.justification: Table 3 adds nine precipitation comparators: ConvPass, FacT-TT, RepAdapter, SCT, Child-TuningD, MoA, HydraLoRA, VeRA, and SAM. New Table 10 also evaluates AdaptFormer+SFAS, LoRA+SFAS, and VPT+SFAS, substantially expanding comparisons with task-selective methods and alternative component combinations.

E3.justification: New vision experiments introduce DINOv2-L segmentation evaluated by mIoU and ImageNet-21k-pretrained ViT-B/16 classification evaluated by accuracy. Table 8 extends component ablations to an increased parameter budget. The original weather splits, training schedules, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged; these are added evaluation designs.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's existing ablations and extreme-weather case study, v2 adds larger-budget component ablations, tests whether generic adapters combined with SFAS can replace TADP, measures computational overhead, and investigates domain specificity through vision experiments. Appendices B.3 and B.5–B.7 substantially broaden the questions tested.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. The new experiments retain point-estimate reporting; references to significant performance differences do not introduce statistical testing.

E6.justification: Matched original weather results remain unchanged, but v2 adds substantial results in Tables 3, 8, and 10–13. Examples include Child-TuningD's 12-hour SEEPS of 0.407 versus the retained WeatherPEFT value of 0.368, and WeatherPEFT's newly reported 70.7% ACDC mean mIoU and 74.0% VTAB-1K accuracy. These are additional comparisons and settings, not improved scores for the original experiments.

T1.justification: The task definitions, TADP equations, Fisher-information derivation, stochastic selection formula, and existing metric definitions are retained. The metric appendix moves from E.5 to F.5. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: WeatherPEFT combines TADP and SFAS for efficient weather-model adaptation, approaches full-tuning performance with fewer parameters, and surpasses full tuning on regional precipitation forecasting. The added evidence does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of limited-budget performance saturation, TADP's value beyond generic adapters combined with SFAS, and the training-time tradeoff. Appendix B.7 newly qualifies performance outside weather and attributes weaker VTAB results to frozen RGB embeddings making prompts effectively static. The original Discussion limitations are retained.

D1.justification: v1 promises a future code release; v2 supplies a repository link and reports that source code and a README cover setup, data preparation, and execution. Table 11 adds method-specific training times. Existing implementation and hyperparameter tables are largely unchanged, and the reported external resources cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: The introduction and related work add a focused distinction between WeatherPEFT's dynamic selection and existing task-selective approaches, including SAM and SCT. References also expand for the added PEFT comparators, vision benchmarks, and weather studies. The overall positioning within weather foundation models and PEFT remains intact.

P1.justification: Selected introduction, related-work, and results passages are expanded, while most existing prose and the main section sequence remain intact. v2 adds acknowledgments, ethics and reproducibility statements, an LLM-use appendix, and publication-status headers; the former implementation and task appendices become E and F.

P2.justification: The tabular presentation expands substantially: Table 3 gains comparator rows, Table 8 gains separate parameter-budget blocks, and new Tables 10–13 display hybrid comparisons, training times, segmentation results, and a wide VTAB task matrix. Existing figures are retained, with Figure 2 relocated and surrounding material reflowed.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central contribution by addressing v1's missing comparisons with close task-selective alternatives and generic adapters equipped with SFAS (Tables 3 and 10). Larger-budget ablations improve component evidence, while training times and vision results expose practical costs and applicability limits. New experiment settings remain incompletely documented, statistical uncertainty is still absent, and the domain-specific mechanism explanation remains inferential, but the stronger comparative validation provides a substantial net improvement.
